OBITUARY REFERENCES 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon'ble Members, this House wishes to place on record 
its heartfelt condolences on the tragic and untimely demise of their Majesties King 
Birendra Bir Bikram Shah Dev, Queen Aishwarya Rajya Laxmi Devi Shah and other 
Members of the Royal Family of Nepal on Friday, the 1SI June, 2001. 
King Birendra was a visionary who will be remembered for his role in 
ushering in a peaceful political change and multi-party democracy in Nepal.  This 
House recalls with deep appreciation his invaluable contribution 
1 

RAJYA SABHA    [23 July, 2001] 
in strengthening the relations with India and in building regional cooperation. The 
people of this country will cherish the memory of his friendship. 
This House do convey our heartfelt sy mpathy and condolence to the people 
of Nepal, His Majesty's Government of Nepal, and to all Members of the Royal Family 
of Nepal. 
Hon'ble Members, I also refer with profound sorrow to the passing away of 
Shri R.K. Narayan, Shri G.Y. Krishnan, Shri Jagan Nath Kaus hal, Shri Mohammad 
Yunus, Shri Niren Ghosh and Shri V.C. Ganesan, former Members of this House. 
Shri R.K. Narayan passed away on 14th May, 2001, at the age of 94. Born at 
Chennai in October, 1906, Shri Narayan ha d his education at Ma haraja's High School 
and Maharaja's College at Mysdre. 
A prolific writer and author of novels  and short stories, Shri Narayan wrote 
about ordinary human beings with extraordin ary insight, sympathy and wit. His novels 
are not only popular but also influential.  The corpus of Narayan's works includes 
novels, stories, essays, travelogues and memoirs. 
Some of the books which won laurel s are "Swami and Friends", "The 
Guide", "The Vendor of Sweets", "The Da rk Room", "Mr.Sampath", "The English 
Teacher" and "Malgudi Days". It is the novel "The Guide" which fetched him the 
Sahitya Academy Award in 1960. His works have been translated into different 
languages, both Indian and foreign, and ar e taught as part of the curriculum in 
literature courses in several countries all over the world. 
Shri Narayan was awarded the Padma Bhushan and was also the Fellow of 
the Royal Society of Literature, United Kingdom and American College, Washington 
DC. He was also a Member of American Academy of Arts and Letters. 
Shri Narayan was a Nominated Member of this House from May, 1986 to 
May, 1992. During his membership in the Rajya Sabha, he spoke once on the burden 
of the schoolbag that school children have to bear, and strongly pleaded for a lighter 
and more sensible curriculum for India's children. 
Although Shri Narayan is no more with us, his vast liter ary and humanistic 
legacy will endure with us. 
2 

 
[23 July, 2001] RAJYA SABHA  
Shri G.Y. Krishnan passed away on 20 May, 2001 at the age of 72, 
Born in October, 1929 at Kolar, Shri Krishnan had his education at Kolar, 
Mysore and Bangalore. An Advocate by vocation, Shri Krishnan was 
associated with various social welfare movements for the uplift of labourers, 
Backward Classes and Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. He started 
several co-operative and industrial so cieties as well as educational and 
training institutes for their benefit. Shri Krishnan was also the Chairman of 
the Coffee Board from 1988 to 1990. 
The legislative career of Shri G.Y. Krishnan started with 
membership of the Fourth Lok Sabha. He  was re-elected to  the Fifth, Sixth 
and Seventh Lok Sabha. He also represen ted the State of Karnataka in this 
House from April, 1990 to April, 1996. During this period, he took keen 
interest in the proceedings of the House.  Shri Krishnan served as the Minister 
of State in the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism in the Union Council 
of Ministers from September, 1995 to May, 1993. 
In the passing away of Shri G.Y. Krishnan, the country has lost an 
eminent Parliamentarian and a devoted social worker. 
Shri Jagan Nath Kaushal passed away on 31 st May, 2001, at the age 
of 86. Born in April, 1915 at Patiala, Shri Kaushal had his education at Patiala 
and Lahore. He started his career as an  Advocate, served as District and 
Sessions Judge in the erstwhile State 0" Patiala and PEPSU from 1947 to 
1949, and he was Additional Judge of the Punjab High Court from 1965 to 
1966. He was Advocate-General of Punjab in 1965 and again in 1967. He also 
served as Advocate-General of Haryana from 1969 to 1976. Shri Kaushal was 
President of the PEPSU High Court Bar Association in 1954 and Punjab High 
Court Bar Association in 196:2. He was Governor of the State of Bihar from 
1976 to 1979. Shri Kaushal represented the State of Punjab in this House for 
two consecutive terms fron April, 1952 to  April, 1958 and again from April, 
1958 to April, 1964. He served as Chairman, House Committee, Rajya Sabha 
from 1962 to 1964. Later, he became a Member of the 7* and 8 m Lok Sabha. 
He also served as the Union Minister  of Law, Justice and Company Affairs 
from 1982 to 1985. 
In the passing away of Shri Kaushal, the country has lost a veteran 
Parliamentarian and an outstanding legal luminary. 
 
 
 
                                      
                                      3 

RAJYA SABHA    [23 July. 2001] 
Shri Mohammad Yunus pa ssed away on the 17 ,th June, 2001, at the 
age of 85. Born at Abbotabad (former North West Frontier Province), in June, 
1916, Shri Yunus had his education at Aligarh and Peshawar. Nephew of 
Frontier Gandhi, Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, Shri Yunus plunged into the 
freedom struggle while still in his student days and was imprisoned during the 
Quit India and the Kashmir Movements.  He was closely associated with 
Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru and Maulana Azad. He joined the Indian 
Foreign Service in 1947 and headed the Indian Diplomatic Missions at Jakarta, 
Ankara, Baghdad, Madrid, San Francisco and Algiers. He played a pivotal 
role in the Non-Aligned Movement Summits at Lusaka, Algiers and Colombo. 
He also served as the Chairman of th e Trade Fair Authority of India from 
January, 1971 to March, 1977 and again from 1980 to 1989. He was also 
Chairman of the Non-Aligned Press Agencies Pool. He was a Nominated 
Member of this House, from June 1989 to June, 1995. 
In the passing away of Shri Mohammad Yunus, the country has lost 
a freedom fighter, an able administrator and an accomplished diplomat. 
Shri Niren Ghosh, an ex-Member of this House passed away in 
Kolkata on the 1s1 July, 2001 at the age of 87. 
Born at Barisal (now in Bangladesh) in October, 1915, Shri Ghosh 
had his education at Barisal and Kolkata. Shri Ghosh joined the freedom 
movement in his school days during 1927-28 and detained without trial 
during 1933-37. Ah active political worker and trade unionist, Shri Ghosh 
actively took part in the Peasant Movement, the Anti-Imperialist Movement 
and was imprisoned on many occasions. He was Secretary of the All India 
Committee of Centre of Indian Trade Un ions and President, Bengal Chatkal 
Majdoor Union and was also connected with diverse unions. 
Shri Ghosh represented the State of West Bengal in this House for 
two terms from April, 1962 to April, 1968 and again from July, 1969 to July, 
1975. During that period he took keen interest in the proceedings of the 
House.   Shri Ghosh was also a Member of the 7th Lok Sabha. 
In the passing away of Shri Ghosh the country has lost a noted 
Parliamentarian, social worker and a veteran trade unionist. 
Shri V.C. Ganesan, an ex-Member of this House passed away at 
Chennai on the 21st July, 2001 at the age of 72 after a prolonged illness. 
Shri Ganesan was born in October, 1928 at South Arcot District, 
Tamil Nadu. An actor from a very young age, Shri Ganesan was conferred the 
title of 'Sivaji' by the late Shri Periyar E.V. Ramaswamy Naicker for his 
4 

[23 July, 2001] RAJYA SABHA  
outstanding performance of the character of Chhatrapati Sivaji. Shri Ganesan 
was the first artiste from India to go to USA under the Cultural Exchange 
Programme of the Government. Shri Ganesan was conferred the title of 
Padmashree in recognition of his charitable and national activities. He was 
also awarded the 'Padma Bhushan" in  1984. A winner of the 'Dada Saheb 
Phalke Award", Shri Ganesan acted in over 175 films. Shri Ganesan was a 
Nominated Member of this House from February, 1982 to April, 1984. 
In the passing away of Shri V.C. Ganesan, the country has lost an 
eminent cine personality. 
Hon. Members, this House also wishes to place on record its 
profound sorrow and grief at the passing  away of Shri S.S.  Bhalerao, former 
Secretary-General of the Rajya Sabha on 30lh May, 2001, at the age of 80. 
Before joining the Rajya Sabha Secreta riat, Shri S.S. Bhalerao 
served in the erstwhile Hyderabad Legislative Assembly as Assistant 
Secretary and later in the erstwhile ^omb ay State Legislative Assembly as its 
Secretary. Shri Bhalerao  joined the Rajya Sabha Secretariat in November, 
1958 and with his vast experience and good judgement, went on to occupy 
the highest position of Secretary-General, Rajya Sabha in April, 1976. He 
built up a loyal and efficient Secretaria t to enable Members to fulfil their 
Parliamentary role adequately. Occupy ing the Secretary-General's Chair for 
five years, Shri Bhalerao set a high standard of service to our Parliament. 
Shri S.S. Bhalerao served this august institution for nearly 23 years 
and helped in moulding and shaping high Parliamentary traditions and was 
instrumental in helping develop new and healthy conventions. 
We deeply mourn the passing away of their Majesties King Birendra 
Bir Bikram Shah Dev, Queen Aishwary a Rajya Laxmi Devi Shah and other 
Members of the  Royal Family of Nepal; Shri R K. Narayan, Shri G.Y. 
Krishnan, Shri Jagan Nath Kaushal, Shri Mohammad Yunus, Shri Niren 
Ghosh, Shri V.C. Ganesan and Shri S.S. Bhalerao. 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a 
mark of respect to the memory of the departed.

REFERENCE REGARDING TRAIN ACCIDENT NEAR KOZHIKODE 
IN  KERALA 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, as you are aware, a great tragedy took 
place on the 22 nd June, 2001, when four bogies of the Mangalore-Chennai Mail 
jumped the tracks and fell into the overflowing Kadalundi river near Kozhikode, in 
Kerala, killing over 50 persons and leaving hund reds of others inju red in the accident. 
The loss of so many precious lives has stunned the whole country. The entire House 
extends its heartfelt condolences to the affected families in their hour of grief and also 
prays for the early recovery of those who have been injured. 
                     I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a mark of 
respect to the memory of those who lost their lives in this tragedy.  
                       (Hon. Members then stood in silence for a minute.) 
REFERENCE REGARDING TRAGIC DEATH OF AMARNATH PILGRIMS 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, it is w ith utmost grief and sorrow that I 
refer to the tragic death of 13 persons, including six pilgrims, during this year's 
Amarnath Yatra, at Sheshnag in Doda district, on 21 s' July, 2001. The Yatra, which 
symbolizes peace and harmony, is, however, continuing and devotees in large numbers 
are visiting the holy shrine. I am sure the whole House will join me in condemning this 
barbaric act which has shocked the entire ci vilised world, and in offering condolences 
to the bereaved families.
